archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (pitching-first)
archetype.definition: A 93-win team built on the league's best staff ERA won its Wild Card round easily, then scored five runs in three games and was swept out of the ALDS by the division rival that had edged it all summer.

report.headline: An A+ rotation carried them to October; the bats vanished against Tampa Bay.

recap.finish: 93-68, second in the AL East; swept BOS 2-0 in the Wild Card, then swept 0-3 by TB in the ALDS
recap.body:
This was a different Yankees team from the one that came before it. The 2025 club led the league in runs and ranked 15th in run prevention. The 2026 version flipped that: second in runs allowed per game, a league-best 3.23 ERA, and an offense that slid to eighth in scoring with an .720 OPS that ranked only 11th. The record barely moved, 93-68 after back-to-back 94-win years, but the way they got there changed. The win came from the mound, and the lineup was a supporting act built around one hitter.

The season had a clear shape. A 4-1 March and a 16-10 April set the pace, and May was the best month for run margin: 152 scored against 101 allowed. Then the bats cooled. June went 12-14 and July managed only 93 runs in 25 games, under four a night, yet the pitching kept July at 14-11 despite a slightly negative run margin. August and September (16-12, then 15-8) restored the cushion. The longest skid was seven games and the longest run eight, so the ups and downs stayed modest.

Cam Schlittler was the engine: a 1.95 ERA backed by a 2.56 FIP, 239 strikeouts, 6.2 WAR and fifth on his position's tab out of 215. Max Fried was nearly as good when he pitched (2.80 ERA, 2.65 FIP), but he made only 20 starts and Gerrit Cole 22, so Will Warren's league-average 156 innings did a lot of the bulk work. That still added up to an A+ rotation. On offense, Ben Rice's 41 homers and 149 wRC+ were the difference between an average lineup and a good one. Luis García Jr. added 30 homers on a thin .309 OBP, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. was worth 3.5 WAR on 41 steals and defense rather than his bat. Catcher, shortstop and the outfield corners were soft spots: Austin Wells (77 wRC+) and José Caballero (83) gave little, and Trent Grisham and Heliot Ramos combined for under one WAR with poor defensive numbers, part of a fielding unit that rated below average.

The record slightly undersold the team. A run differential that ranked fourth implied about two and a half more wins, but even that would not have caught Tampa Bay, which finished 4.5 games clear. October started perfectly: Boston was beaten 9-0 and 9-2 at home. Then the offense disappeared against the Rays. The Yankees lost 1-0 and 5-2 on the road and 4-3 at home. That was five runs in three games, two of the losses by a single run, while the staff kept every game within reach. Rice hit four postseason homers with a 321 wRC+. Bellinger (38), Grisham (-9) and Chisholm (51) gave almost nothing around him.

The postseason table makes it look worse in hindsight: the best run differential of the 12 playoff teams and a 1.88 ERA, which still got them only two wins. It was the third straight 93-94 win season, and the formula that produced it here was a dominant staff and one great bat. That was enough for October but not enough to survive a series where the bat around him went cold.

highlights.title: Schlittler fronts an A+ rotation
highlights.body: Schlittler's 1.95 ERA was no fluke. His 2.56 FIP and 31.4% strikeout rate say he earned it, and he was the biggest reason the staff ERA led the league. Fried's 2.65 FIP confirms a second true front-line arm. The group's strength should carry over, though it leaned on 193-plus innings from one pitcher and limited starts from Fried and Cole.

highlights.title: Ben Rice carried the lineup
highlights.body: Rice was the only hitter in the regular group above 125 wRC+, producing 41 homers and 4.3 WAR from the DH spot. He was even better in October, with four homers and nine RBI in five games. His .363 OBP paired with power is the profile of a genuine middle-of-the-order bat, not a hot year.

highlights.title: Headrick and Bednar locked down late innings
highlights.body: Brent Headrick (2.18 ERA, 2.46 FIP, 29 holds) and David Bednar (35 saves, 2.61 FIP) were both top-20 relievers on the tab. Their peripherals match their results, so this end of the bullpen looks repeatable. Neither allowed a run in the postseason.

lowlights.title: Five runs in a three-game ALDS
lowlights.body: After 18 runs against Boston, the offense scored 0, 2 and 3 against Tampa Bay and lost two of the three games by one run. It was the regular season's flaw in miniature: when Rice is not the one doing damage, there is little behind him. Three postseason games is a tiny sample, but the thin lineup was real all year.

lowlights.title: Lineup holes at C, SS, corners
lowlights.body: Team OPS ranked 11th, and July produced fewer than four runs a game. Wells and Caballero were well below average at the plate, and Grisham and Ramos rated poorly in the field while hitting just below average. This is the clearest drop from the 2025 offense that led the league, and it will not fix itself.

lowlights.title: Middle relief outran its peripherals
lowlights.body: Paul Blackburn led the bullpen in innings with a 1.59 ERA but a 3.75 FIP and a 20.5% strikeout rate. John Schreiber's 3.28 ERA sat on a 4.62 FIP, and he rated below replacement. The B- bullpen grade is closer to the truth than those ERAs, and regression is likely if the same arms soak up those innings.

arc.note: A fast start through May gave way to a June-July sag when the offense cooled, and the pitching kept July winning anyway. A 15-8 September, including three of four at home against Tampa Bay, finished the regular season on its best month.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is the pitching: Schlittler's numbers are backed by his peripherals, Fried's FIP says he is an ace when available, and Headrick and Bednar give the bullpen a trustworthy back end. The concern is innings, since Fried and Cole combined for 42 starts and Warren's average work filled the gap. The lineup is where the work is. Rice and García Jr. supply the power, and Chisholm and Bellinger the all-around value, but catcher, shortstop and both outfield corners graded poorly, and the team fell from first to eighth in scoring in a year. Luck was not a big factor. The run differential says the team was a couple of wins better than its record, while the middle-relief ERAs say the bullpen was a bit worse than it looked. A club with this staff should contend again, but the ALDS showed what happens when one bat has to carry the offense.

confidence.note: Full 161-game season with consistent underlying stats; the postseason judgments rest on just five games.
